description: At the 2026-06-17 FOMC — Kevin Warsh's first meeting as Fed Chair — the Committee held the target range at 3.50-3.75% (unanimous 12-0) but flipped its forward guidance HAWKISH: the median dot for end-2026 rose to 3.8% (from 3.4% in March), REMOVING the prior outlook for a 2026 cut and signaling at least one HIKE is now seen as likely. Post-meeting, traders began pricing a hike as early as October. The statement attributes elevated inflation in part to supply shocks driving energy prices (the Iran/Hormuz conflict) and notes solid growth, strong capex/productivity, and a labor market keeping pace (the strong May jobs print). This is a regime shift from the disinflation-cut path the market had assumed: long-duration/rate-sensitive equities (grid/utilities, solar, real estate) face a higher-for-longer discount-rate headwind, the USD/DXY is supported, and gold faces a higher-real-rate headwind partly offset by its stagflation/energy-shock hedge bid.
user_notes: Registered 2026-06-29 in the scan refresh. The hawkish dot-plot flip is the single biggest macro regime change since the last review (2026-06-12): the Fed went from a hold-with-a-cut-bias to a hold-with-a-HIKE-bias, with an Oct hike now in play. Cross-cutting macro catalyst (not tied to one structural). Transmission: (1) HEADWIND to long-duration/rate-sensitive books we hold conviction in — grid_infrastructure (mov_20260604 grid position), solar, real_estate; risk_discipline rate-stops on those movements should be re-read. (2) USD support — a yfinance-priced EURUSD invalidation stop on the copper movement (inv_04) is rate-linked. (3) Gold: net-ambiguous (real-rate headwind vs energy-shock/stagflation hedge), consistent with gold's pullback to ~$4,187 from its ATH. Linked to the Hormuz energy shock (the inflation source the Fed is reacting to) and to the 06-05 selloff (which already had a yields/jobs leg). is_priced_in 0.5: yields moved on the day; the actual Oct-hike decision is unresolved.

review_log.evidence: Thesis realised: FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0); 2026-10-07 minutes say another hike is likely by year end; hot September CPI on 2026-10-14 (3.7% vs 3.6% expected; core 2.6% vs 2.5%) lifted October-hike odds from ~20% to 37-50% and December is priced ~81%; 10y ~5.2-5.3%. sector_impact BACKFILLED this scan (it was unstated, so the scorer assumed supportive on nine sectors, including +14.3 of CA for eu_retail_banking and oil_majors_integrated that rested entirely on this event): adverse for oil_majors_integrated (5%+ Treasuries compete with dividend yield, stronger USD) and for the long-duration/financed sectors, supportive only for eu_retail_banking. The oil_majors direction is the lowest-confidence call: the energy shock that CAUSED the hawkishness is supportive for majors but is carried by cat_20260817_hormuz_reescalation, not by this event.
review_log.source: Schwab FOMC recap 2026-09-16; CNBC FOMC minutes 2026-10-07; XTB / investingLive CPI wraps 2026-10-14

review_log.evidence: August CPI (released 2026-09-11) held above the Fed's 2% target; CME/Polymarket odds of a 25bp HIKE at the 2026-09-15/16 FOMC rose to ~85-90% (from ~55% at Jackson Hole, per the 2026-08-31 review_log entry). This is now corroborated by an ACTUAL action, not just guidance: the ECB hiked 25bp on 2026-09-10 (its second hike since the Iran war began, registered separately as cat_20260910_ecb_rate_hike) on euro-area inflation of 3.3% YoY, and the BoJ is priced at 62% odds of a further 25bp hike at its 2026-09-17/18 meeting, with board member Masu explicitly reaffirming a continued-hiking stance. Three major central banks moving in the same 10-day window on the same energy-shock driver is the confirmation this catalyst's thesis needed: the disinflation-cut path is not just paused, it has reversed into synchronized tightening.
review_log.source: Bloomberg/Chase/Forbes Fed coverage 2026-09-05/12; ECB monetary policy statement 2026-09-10; Bloomberg BoJ Masu remarks 2026-09-10

review_log.evidence: Fed held at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth consecutive meeting in July 2026, and Chair Warsh used Jackson Hole to flag that underlying inflation is NOT slowing; CME FedWatch put roughly 55% odds on a 25bp HIKE at the September meeting vs ~45% hold - the market is now pricing a hike, not a cut. Corroborated by the ECB, which raised all three key rates 25bp on 2026-06-11 (first hike in three years, effective 2026-06-17) on energy-driven inflation. NOTE: search results for US CPI were contaminated by September-2024 articles quoting 2.5% headline; the 2026-dated sources put CPI nearer 3.5% YoY. The 2.5% figure was NOT used.
review_log.source: Jackson Hole remarks (Warsh) via Yahoo Finance/Motley Fool Aug 2026; ECB monetary policy decisions 2026-06-11 and 2026-07-23
